name: MIL-STD-810H Method 503.7 Procedure I-D temperature shock between a -46 C cold-region exterior and an 18-24 C heated enclosure, transfer within one minute
plain_name: Carry a military device between arctic outdoors and a heated shelter to check sudden temperature change does not crack it
description: Ground-transfer temperature shock per MIL-STD-810H Method 503.7 (Procedure I-D, shocks to and from controlled ambient): the item is stabilized at the cold-region exterior extreme, selected from Method 502.7 Table 502.7-I Cold (C2) = -46 C, and transferred in no more than one minute to the cold-regions enclosure condition of 18-24 C at 30-50 % RH (and back), stabilizing after each transfer. The method calls for two chambers or a two-celled chamber that re-stabilizes within five minutes after transfer.
keywords: Carry a military device between arctic outdoors and a heated shelter to check sudden temperature change does not crack it

sources.citation: MIL-STD-810H Method 503.7 Temperature Shock (Department of Defense Test Method Standard, 31 January 2019)
MIL-STD-810H Method 502.7 Low Temperature (Department of Defense Test Method Standard, 31 January 2019)

requirements.rationale: The (two-zone) machine must provide both the -46 C cold extreme and the 24 C upper end of the heated-enclosure condition (227.15-297.15 K).
The cold side must reach the Method 502.7 Cold (C2) ambient extreme of -46 C (227.15 K), which Method 503.7 says to select from the 502.7 tables for cold-region ground transfer.
The heated-enclosure condition carries 30-50 % RH; humidity control is optional for the shock itself.
